notes: Read SKILL.md and references/pipeline-syntax.md in full. The skill shows how to write Jenkins declarative and scripted pipelines: Docker, Kubernetes and labeled agents, parameters, credentials binding, parallel stages, shared libraries, plugin lists, JCasC configuration and multibranch pipelines.

The output is Jenkinsfile/JCasC content the agent writes into the user's repository; `sh` steps (npm, make, ./deploy.sh, docker login, git push) run inside the user's Jenkins, not on the agent's machine. Credentials come from Jenkins credential IDs or ${ADMIN_PASSWORD}/${DOCKER_PASSWORD} variables; nothing is hardcoded.

Review before adopting: the Kubernetes agent runs docker:24-dind with privileged: true (SKILL.md:121-124); the git push example embeds ${GH_TOKEN} in the remote URL (SKILL.md:203) and `docker login -p` (pipeline-syntax.md:126) can expose secrets in logs — prefer credential helpers or --password-stdin. Related Skills (SKILL.md:435-437) link to sibling skills ../github-actions/, ../../orchestration/kubernetes-ops/ and ../../containers/docker-management/ as optional reading only.
